```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 0.3)

# draws n full-width blank lines (margin to margin) for handwritten answers,
# as a single plot so spacing is deterministic; pair with fig.height = 0.3 * n
blank_lines <- function(n = 1) {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, n), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    segments(0, n - i + 0.5, 1, n - i + 0.5, lwd = 1)
  }
}

# reserves blank work space (no ruled lines) for equation manipulation /
# show-your-work; pair with fig.height set to however much room is needed
blank_space <- function() {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  plot.new()
}
```

```{r key-helpers, include=FALSE}
ans_col <- rgb(200, 0, 130, maxColorValue = 255)
# redraws blank_table() so cells flagged TRUE in `ans` use the answer color
blank_table <- function(headers, body, col_widths = NULL,
                        header_height = 0.35, row_height = 0.5,
                        cex = 0.95, bold_rows = integer(0), ans = NULL) {
  nc <- length(headers); nr <- length(body)
  if (is.null(col_widths)) col_widths <- rep(1, nc)
  col_widths <- col_widths / sum(col_widths)
  cx <- c(0, cumsum(col_widths))
  h_total <- header_height + nr * row_height
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0), family = "serif")
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, h_total), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "",
       xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i")
  y <- h_total
  segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = 1.5)
  y <- y - header_height
  segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = 1.5)
  for (i in seq_len(nr)) {
    y <- y - row_height
    segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = if (i == nr) 1.5 else 0.5,
             col = if (i == nr) "black" else "grey70")
  }
  for (v in cx) segments(v, 0, v, h_total, lwd = 1)
  yh <- h_total - header_height / 2
  for (j in seq_len(nc)) text((cx[j] + cx[j + 1]) / 2, yh, labels = headers[[j]], font = 2, cex = cex)
  y <- h_total - header_height
  for (i in seq_len(nr)) {
    yc <- y - row_height / 2
    for (j in seq_len(nc)) {
      val <- body[[i]][[j]]
      is_ans <- !is.null(ans) && isTRUE(ans[[i]][[j]])
      if (!identical(val, "")) text((cx[j] + cx[j + 1]) / 2, yc, labels = val, cex = cex,
                                    font = if (i %in% bold_rows) 2 else 1,
                                    col = if (is_ans) ans_col else "black")
    }
    y <- y - row_height
  }
}
```

\ans{\textbf{Answer key.} Answers are in magenta.}


# NRES 746 -- Week 1, Lecture 1: Math & Stats Self-Diagnostic

&nbsp;


&nbsp;

This is **not graded**, but will be collected at the end of class. There are no wrong
answers -- the goal is just to take stock of the tools you're bringing into this class,
and to see which ones might need a bit of dusting off. Some of these are meant to make
you think a little!

**Instructions:** Work alone for about 5 minutes. Don't worry if you get stuck --
just note where you got stuck and move on. After 5 minutes, compare answers with a
neighbor for a few minutes.

## Part 1: Logarithms & exponents

**1a.** Solve for x: $2^x = 32$

x = \ans{5}

**1b.** A population grows according to $N_t = N_0 e^{rt}$. If $N_0 = 100$ and
$N_t = 550$ after $t = 8$ years, solve for the growth rate $r$:

r = \ans{$\ln(550/100)/8 = \ln(5.5)/8 \approx 0.213$ per year}

&nbsp;

## Part 2: Derivatives & integrals

**2a.** If $f(x) = (4x^2 - 3x)^5$, what is $f'(x)$?

$f'(x) =$ \ans{$5(4x^2 - 3x)^4(8x - 3)$}

&nbsp;

**2b.** Evaluate $f'(x)$ from **2a** at $x = 1$:

$f'(1) =$ \ans{$5(1)^4(5) = 25$}

In one sentence, what does this number tell you about the function $f(x)$ at $x = 1$?

\ans{The slope of $f$ at $x = 1$: $f$ is increasing there, by about 25 units of $f$ per unit of $x$.}

&nbsp;

**2c.** A recruitment rate for a population is given by $r(t) = 4t$ (new individuals per unit time).

First, find the antiderivative $R(t) = \displaystyle\int 4t \, dt$:

$R(t) =$ \ans{$2t^2 + C$}

Now use $R(t)$ to compute the total number of new recruits between $t=0$ and $t=5$:

$\displaystyle\int_0^5 4t \, dt = R(5) - R(0) =$ \ans{$2(25) - 0 = 50$}

&nbsp;

## Part 3: Probability

**3a.** $P(A) = 0.4$, $P(B) = 0.5$, and $P(A \text{ and } B) = 0.2$. What is
$P(A \text{ or } B)$?

\ans{$0.4 + 0.5 - 0.2 = 0.7$}

**3b.** A family has two children. You are told that at least one of them is a girl.
What is the probability that *both* children are girls? Briefly show your reasoning
(consider all the equally likely possibilities for two children).

\ans{$1/3$. The equally likely families are GG, GB, BG, BB; "at least one girl" rules out BB, leaving GG, GB, BG, of which one is GG.}

## Part 4: Confidence intervals & p-values

**4a.** Circle the interpretation you think is *most correct* for a 95% confidence
interval on a mean:

  a) There is a ~95% probability that the true mean falls within this particular interval.
  b) About 95% of the intervals we compute from random samples would contain the true mean.
  c) 95% of the data fall within this interval.

\ans{(b)}

**4b.** Circle the definition you think is *most correct* for a p-value:

  a) The probability that the null hypothesis is true.
  b) The probability of observing results at least as 'extreme' under the null hypothesis.
  c) The probability that the alternative hypothesis is false.

\ans{(b)}

## Part 5: R / pseudocode

**5.** Each snippet below has exactly one error. Circle it and write your
correction directly on the snippet.

**5a.** Bracket notation

```

site_data <- matrix(c(12, 7, 19, 4, 45, 23, 61, 15), nrow = 4, ncol = 2)
# Extract the entire second column
site_data[2]

```

\ans{\texttt{site\_data[, 2]} (\texttt{site\_data[2]} returns only the second element.)}

**5b.** For loops

```

values <- c(10, 20, 30, 40)
doubled <- numeric(length(values))
for (i in values) {
  doubled[i] <- values[i] * 2
}

```

\ans{\texttt{for (i in seq\_along(values))} (the loop should run over positions 1 to 4, not the values 10 to 40).}

**5c.** Function syntax

```

GetRange <- function(x)
  max_val <- max(x)
  min_val <- min(x)
  max_val - min_val

```

\ans{The function body needs curly braces: \texttt{function(x) \{} \ldots\ \texttt{\}}. Without them, only the first line belongs to the function.}
